Forecast Discussion

An upper-level low passed north of us this morning and moves north-northeast to near Lake Ontario by sunset. A moist west-to-northwest flow on its south side crosses the mountains through tonight.

Snow showers and flurries continue today, mostly on the west side of the Appalachians. They increase a little this evening and taper to flurries after midnight. Clouds begin to decrease toward sunrise. Gusty winds last through this evening and ease late at night.

Most of the western half of the mountain region picks up a dusting to 1" of snow. The higher elevations west are a different world, with 1" to 4" and isolated higher totals at the highest elevations in the extreme northwest corner of North Carolina.

High pressure builds over the Southeast Saturday. The day starts cold and gusty, then winds ease and the afternoon is not as cold under high clouds.

Sunday, low pressure moves from Arkansas toward the Great Lakes and pulls a cold front toward us. Morning sunshine gives way to afternoon clouds. Rain is possible by sunset, especially west, and falls everywhere Sunday evening.

Colder air follows after midnight on gusty northwest winds. Rain changes to snow showers and flurries, mostly west. Flurries are possible Monday morning before skies clear in the afternoon.

High pressure settles in for the rest of the week with dry weather. It is cool Tuesday but noticeably warmer Wednesday and Thursday. Clouds thicken Thursday night as low pressure organizes over the southern Plains. Rain returns next Friday.
